correctness.rationale: Coordinate-sign averaging reduces every quadratic Euclidean pullback to a diagonal form without worsening its two-sided comparison constants. For a diagonal form the entire unit sphere becomes \(F_r(t)=r t^{4/3}+(1-t)^{2/3}\). Its derivative gives either no critical point or exactly the symmetric pair \(u,1-u\). The endpoint and critical values are explicit, and the distortion has three exhaustive regimes. The relevant ratios have derivatives of fixed sign on \(0<u<1/2\), forcing the unique optimum at the contact transition \(m_c(u)=r\). This transition reduces to \(z^3+z^2+z-1=0\). A nonzero cross term strictly raises one signed value at the maximizing contact while the axis keeps the old minimum available, excluding every tilted optimum.

value.rationale: The pair \((3/2,3)\) is the first canonical Hölder-conjugate mixed-power Musielak--Orlicz plane whose exponents lie on opposite sides of the Hilbert exponent. Unlike the already-covered superquadratic regime, the Euclidean circle is not optimal; the exact anisotropic distance is governed by a nontrivial three-contact transition and a cubic algebraic parameter. This gives a natural benchmark for cross-Hilbert variable-exponent geometry rather than an arbitrary numerical slice.
